title: DeepMind unveils Genie 4 world model promising more realistic physics and humans
gist: DeepMind's Genie 4 world model adds native audio including speech, better physics and people, steered by Gemini 3.8 Flash, with access starting through the $100-per-month AI Ultra plan and the Gemini API, but worlds stay consistent only for minutes.

insights.claim: Genie 4 uses Gemini 3.8 Flash as a guiding agent to break down goals and evaluate each frame, helping keep simulations on track.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: Coupling world models with LLM agents is the architecture trend.
insights.locator: Paragraph beginning "When you prompt a world"

insights.claim: Genie 4 worlds still stay consistent for only a couple of minutes before forgetting how things started.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: Memory limit constrains uses such as training environments and games.
insights.quote: only remain consistent for a couple of minutes
insights.locator: Paragraph beginning "When you prompt a world"

insights.claim: Genie 4 improves aerodynamics and collisions and more natural human movement, and is the first DeepMind world model with native audio, including interactive speech.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: Realistic speech raised AI video realism; a similar shift could follow in world models.

insights.claim: DeepMind frames world models as a key step toward AGI, usable for infinite training environments for robots and rapid prototyping in creative fields.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: Synthetic environments for robotics training are the big option value.

insights.claim: Genie 3's reveal last year sent gaming stocks tumbling, and world models have since become a major focus of AI labs.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: Gaming equities react to world-model releases; Genie 4 may repeat this.

insights.claim: Genie 4 will come via the Gemini API and AI Studio with pricing unannounced, and for consumers first through AI Ultra plans starting at $100 per month, with a waitlist and no timeline.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: Compute-heavy product launching at premium tier first.
